keywords.rule: Counts are papers whose title or abstract contains one of the keyword's phrases (porter-stemmed, as the theme trends); the baseline is the papers in scope first submitted in the 12 weeks before the issue, its own papers excluded. new: fewer than 5 baseline papers; rising: at least 5 papers and a rate at least 1.5 times the baseline rate; hot: at least 15 papers (and 1% of the issue) at a rate at least 0.67 times the baseline rate; steady: otherwise.
keywords.score: log2(1 + n) · log2(1 + (n + 3) / (E + 3)), E = issue papers × (baseline papers with the phrase + 0.5) / baseline papers

themes.name: Multimodal Safety and Adversarial Attacks
themes.summary: The papers investigate safety and adversarial vulnerabilities across multimodal and embodied AI systems, spanning robot control, vision-language-action models, MLLMs, audio agents, and generative recommenders. They analyze attacks such as jailbreaks, backdoors, poisoning, physical adversarial textures, and harmful content evasion, alongside defenses including unlearning, red-teaming, certified detection, and safety benchmarks. They differ in threat surface and evaluation setting, from scene semantics and memory formation to robot faces, navigation collisions, and tool-calling ethics.

themes.name: Agent Harness Self-Evolution
themes.summary: The papers investigate self-evolution of agent harnesses—the external scaffolding that manages inputs, tools, memory, and execution—through iterative modification guided by feedback. They propose diverse approaches such as predictive improvement models, harness-native training loops, measurement-gated evolution, multi-objective composition, and recursive harnessing, while also providing benchmarks and diagnostic studies that test whether gains reflect reusable procedures rather than task-specific fixes. Key differences include single- versus multi-agent focus, the type of feedback used (outcome, process, or evidence), and application domains like coding, video, and office tasks.

themes.name: Model Merging and Compression
themes.summary: This theme covers methods for merging fine-tuned models and compressing large models through pruning, quantization, low-rank approximation, and lossless coding. Papers differ by target architecture (e.g., Mixture-of-Experts, LoRA, vision transformers, video autoencoders) and by whether they focus on weight-space merging, post-training compression, or hardware-aware codec placement. Several also examine robustness, calibration, or security aspects of these operations.

themes.name: Vision-Language-Action Robot Policies
themes.summary: The papers in this theme build vision-language-action policies that map visual observations and language instructions to continuous robot actions, spanning manipulation, navigation, and driving. They differ in where they intervene: some reshape representations or training objectives (perception-action bridging, hierarchical self-refinement, precision forcing, force specialization), others improve inference and coordination (test-time verified sampling, asynchronous execution, learned adapters for multi-agent teams), and others embed VLM reasoning into planning or navigation. Several focus on generalizing learned skills to new task, scene, or object configurations.

themes.name: World Action Models for Embodied Control
themes.summary: The papers in this theme build world models that predict future latent or visual states and couple that prediction with action generation for embodied control, spanning robot manipulation, GUI agents, driving, and surgical robotics. They differ in how futures are represented (Gaussian-mixture latent prediction, spectral similarity kernels, symplectic Hamiltonian flows, discrete visual tokens, or video generation), in how actions are conditioned or decoded (latent bridge queries, chunk-wise flow matching, one-step action generation, hierarchical multi-timescale designs), and in what they prioritize, such as memory and long-horizon reliability, causal rather than merely plausible futures, proprioceptive closed-loop policy evaluation, or reduced latency.

themes.name: Long-Horizon Agentic Task Benchmarks
themes.summary: The papers construct benchmarks that test whether LLM agents can sustain coherent, tool-using action across extended workflows, spanning terminal operations, scientific data curation, causal investigation, business-request delivery, multi-database querying, memory upkeep, survival sandboxes, and protocol-secured multi-agent coordination. They differ in emphasis: some reward process-level sustained progress rather than a final pass, some stress executable task contracts, memory representation decisions, or skill composition for verifiability, and others evaluate end-to-end protocol risk and robustness. Several also examine environment fidelity and grading validity, from re-executing coding-agent evaluations to grounding agents in real skill specifications and interactive physical environments.

themes.name: Conformal Prediction and Uncertainty
themes.summary: The papers address uncertainty quantification and calibration, proposing methods like conformal prediction, calibrated decision models, and finite-sample control for reliable predictions. They differ in application domains (LLM judging, radiomics, robot navigation, signal temporal logic) and technical focus, such as distribution-free coverage, sequential testing, or optimal transport for prediction sets.

themes.name: Test-Time Compute and Inference Scaling
themes.summary: The papers explore methods for improving model performance by allocating additional computation at inference time, spanning adaptive depth in looped transformers, test-time adaptation for time series and vision-language-action models, verifier-guided scaling for continuous generation, and speculative decoding for efficient MoE inference. They differ in whether they adapt model architecture, decoding strategy, or post-hoc verifier, and in the modalities and constraints they target, such as energy efficiency, memory limits, and real-time full-duplex speech. Some focus on theoretical decoding rules like tilted temperature, while others consolidate test-time gains into the model itself.

themes.name: Flow Matching Generative Modeling
themes.summary: The papers develop flow matching and related continuous-time generative modeling for diverse tasks such as virtual-cell perturbation prediction, fMRI encoding and synthesis, cyclic peptide design, audio codec translation, ocean modeling, and few-step 3D generation. They differ by extending flow matching with posterior uncertainty, token-wise classifier-free guidance, constrained inference-time optimal control, sampling error correction, backprop-free equilibrium propagation training, or Schrödinger bridge transport.

themes.name: Humanoid Locomotion and Whole-Body Control
themes.summary: These papers develop whole-body controllers and locomotion policies for humanoid robots, covering free-space motion tracking, terrain traversal without motion priors, competitive table tennis, cooperative manipulation, high-speed sprinting, and rigid-soft hybrid links, alongside related quadrupedal loco-manipulation. They differ in whether they depend on retargeted motion-capture priors versus learned or planner-based references, and in their control interfaces such as object interaction layers, landing targets, and commander-executor hierarchies.

themes.name: KV Cache Compression and Reuse
themes.summary: The papers compress or reuse KV caches to cut memory and compute in long-context autoregressive generation, spanning LLMs, video, edge, and multi-agent settings. They differ in technique—quantization, eviction, consolidation, cross-model transport, or repair—and in challenges addressed, such as error accumulation, behavior preservation, and cross-model incompatibility.

themes.name: Diffusion Language Models
themes.summary: These papers study diffusion language models (DLMs) for parallel text generation, tackling their degradation with fewer sampling steps, efficient timestep placement, and controllability through anchors. They also extend the paradigm to multimodal co-generation via continuous bitstream diffusion and to securing agentic workflows with constrained diffusion agents. They differ in focus: some propose generation frameworks such as coarse-to-fine modeling, while others analyze optimization, security enforcement, or unified multimodal training.

highlights.why: Achieves 100% attack success rate on all evaluated LLMs via black-box evolutionary red-teaming, a sobering safety result.

Under our protocol, REPRO reaches 100% ASR on AdvBench, JailbreakBench, and HarmBench across 36 target models from 11 families, with a median of 24 target queries per behavior.

highlights.title: Long-Horizon-Terminal-Bench 2.0: Automating Diverse Task Construction and Measuring Sustained Agent Progress
highlights.authors: Zongxia Li, Zhongzhi Li, Yucheng Shi et al.
highlights.why: Extends a benchmark with automated construction and longer horizons, enabling measurement of sustained agent progress.
highlights.key_result: LHTB 2.0 contains 77 tasks across 13 domains and eight task types, preserving the 46 original tasks and adding 31. Across 1,145 scored model-task runs from 15 frontier models, GPT-6-astra leads with dense mean reward 0.69 and 37 tasks at R at least 0.95, and on the 30 reconstruction tasks binary verifier scores average 0.221 whereas dense ladder scores average 0.653.
evidence: We present Long-Horizon-Terminal-Bench 2.0 (LHTB 2.0), an extension of Long-Horizon-Terminal-Bench that preserves its 46 original tasks while correcting task and evaluation-infrastructure defects and extending 31 tasks. LHTB 2.0 contains 77 tasks across 13 domains and eight task types.

Across 1,145 scored model-task runs from 15 frontier models, GPT-6-astra leads with dense mean reward 0.69 and 37 tasks at R at least 0.95, followed by GPT-5.6-sol with dense mean reward 0.67 and 32 tasks at the same threshold.
On the 30 reconstruction tasks, binary verifier scores average 0.221, whereas dense ladder scores average 0.653, showing that outcome-only evaluation discards substantial intermediate progress.

Across 15 frontier models evaluated with a shared terminus-2 agent, the strongest model, GPT-6-astra, resolves only 48.1% of tasks (37/77) at R 0.95, while only 192 of 1,145 scored runs (16.8%) pass overall.

news.title: Higgsfield takes AI video from 1 minute to over 10
news.summary: Higgsfield AI reports that with GPT-6 Astra, user-created videos went from topping out at around one minute to over 10 minutes long, and that GPT-Image-2.5 reliably renders text and infographics over imagery. The company builds its product with about 200 creatives and 100 engineers, says its YouTube channel has almost half a million subscribers, and is targeting "voice to movie" with GPT-Live-1.

news.title: Developing Gemini 4 Argon responsibly and safely
news.summary: Google DeepMind published its safety and security approach for Gemini 4 Argon, which it says solved all 12 end-to-end simulated cyberattack scenarios versus five for the previous generation, with adversarial-set violations reduced nearly twofold. It describes three layers of real-time protection (input screening, internal introspection via activation probes, and continuous monitoring) and cites Wiz using Argon to uncover a critical bug in hospital software affecting hundreds of thousands of patient records, with the Fairwind Program expanding to more trusted cyber defenders.

news.title: Gemini 4 Argon for Robotics
news.summary: Google DeepMind reports Gemini 4 Argon scores 87% on the Embodied Reasoning (ERQA) benchmark, outperforming other frontier models using pure reasoning. The post lists robotics prompts including controlling a Boston Dynamics Spot (12-DoF legs + 6-DoF arm), retargeting human video onto a 76-DoF bimanual humanoid with 22-DoF five-fingered hands, arranging five Scrabble tiles (G, R, A, N, O), and verifying 6/6 target knockdown in a mujoco_warp scene exported as a Blender 4.5 Cycles render.

news.title: Gemini 4 Argon: Built to solve your hardest problems
news.summary: Google DeepMind made Gemini 4 Argon globally available via the API in AI Studio and the Gemini platform, in Google Antigravity for AI Ultra subscribers, and in the Gemini app and AI Mode in Search, at an introductory price of $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens with cached input at 95% off. Cited uses include a Chrome architectural refactor separating core webpage handling from a ~6 million line legacy folder inside Chromium's 40 million-line codebase, ADK optimizations cutting in-memory session prep time by 40% and speeding cold imports by 21%, xTB speedups of up to 2.3x and 1.8x, and a 2.85x inference speedup on an A100 via vLLM on Gemma 4 E2B (from ~37,900 to over 108,000 tokens per second).

news.title: Gemini 4 Argon: Built to solve your hardest problems
news.summary: Google made Gemini 4 Argon globally available for developers and enterprises via the API in AI Studio and the Gemini platform, for AI Ultra subscribers in Google Antigravity, and for Ultra and Pro subscribers in the Gemini app and AI Mode in Search, priced at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens with cached input at 95% off, and ranking #1 on the Vals Index. news.title: All Systems Go: Global PC App Ecosystem Ready for NVIDIA RTX Spark
news.summary: NVIDIA announced RTX Spark, a PC superchip with up to 128GB of unified memory and 1 petaflop of AI compute, with RTX Spark laptops available Friday, Oct. 16. Announced updates include the NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B model on Thursday, Oct. 15, up to 2x performance coming to Adobe apps, NVIDIA Broadcast 2.3 with Video Super Resolution and Frame Generation, a 2x faster DLSS 5 AI model on Oct. 16, DLSS Ray Reconstruction in Blender 5.3 in November, the Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B 4GB SLM on Oct. 23, and local LLM downloads already 5x higher than all of last year.

news.title: NVIDIA Announces New Investments in France’s Startups
news.summary: NVIDIA announced planned new investments in Doctolib, Entalpic, Genesis AI and Pigment, having previously invested in Alice&Bob, Gradium and Scintil Photonics, with nearly $10 billion committed across Europe. The post cites Bull extending European AI server production to NVIDIA Vera Rubin Ultra NVL72 systems planned for 2028 with the Angers factory inaugurated Friday, Oct. 2, the $1 billion 50-satellite Altair-1 constellation launched this month flying NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin modules running Mistral models, and Twake.ai on NVIDIA Nemotron as the sole referenced sovereign digital workplace for more than 2,500 French public organizations.

news.title: How to Rewrite Apache Spark UDFs for GPU Acceleration with AI Agents
news.summary: NVIDIA described rewriting Apache Spark user-defined functions for GPU acceleration using cuDF skills and AI agents, reporting 22x+ speedups and that one rewrite cut operator time from 274.55 to 12.78 hours across a 600-billion-row workload. A major consumer technology company converted more than 30 production UDFs using the workflow, which targets Spark SQL expressions, the RapidsUDF interface for the Java API for cuDF, or custom CUDA kernels via JNI.

news.title: NVIDIA Run:ai Is Now Open Source as Part of NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform
news.summary: NVIDIA released the full NVIDIA Run:ai platform as open source as part of the NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform, with four independently adoptable components: KAI Scheduler, GPU Fractioning Operator, KAI Resource Management, and Workload Map. Eight DSX ecosystem partners including Crusoe, Mirantis, Nebius, OpenNebula Systems, Rafay, Saturn Cloud, Spectro Cloud and vCluster are integrating it, and the complete stack is available on NGC as a Community Product with a Helm chart.

news.title: Run fast, private agents on-device with LFM2.5-24B-A2B
news.summary: Hugging Face released LFM2.5-24B-A2B, a 24B-parameter reasoning model with 2B active parameters per token, built from LFM2-24B-A2B with 40 layers, 64 experts per MoE block and top-4 routing, a context window extended from 32K to 131K tokens, and a vocabulary expanded from 65K to 128K tokens. It scores 48.09 on LiveClaw versus 38.19 for Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, runs at 184 tok/s on an Apple M5 Max and up to 21K output tok/s on a single NVIDIA B300 GPU, with pre-training scaled from ~17T to ~33T tokens plus 2T mid-training tokens at 32K context and 300B at 131K context.

news.title: Building agents that transact with Anchor Browser and AgentCore payments
news.summary: Anchor Browser with Agentic Payments, developed with the AWS Generative AI Innovation Center Partner Agent Factory, is now available on AWS Marketplace and integrates with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore payments so agents can pay for x402-protected pages and APIs. The x402 protocol is described as an open standard for HTTP-based machine-to-machine payments in which a server returns HTTP 402 Payment Required with the amount, accepted payment methods and payment address; AgentCore payments manages wallet connectivity, enforces spending limits, and logs payment activity through Amazon CloudWatch.

news.title: Manage private pricing offers for Amazon Bedrock with managed entitlements
news.summary: AWS described two ways to activate AWS Marketplace Private Pricing Offer entitlements for Amazon Bedrock in AWS License Manager: a lightweight script for one-time activation requiring --apply --confirm-account-id, and an event-driven AWS CDK path for ongoing automation with a seller allowlist. Organization-level grants are auto-accepted but remain Disabled until activated; the CDK stack listens on the default event bus in us-east-1 for events with source aws.agreement-marketplace.

news.title: Natural language security queries at Orca Security using Amazon Bedrock
news.summary: Orca Security built Discovery AI, a natural language query agent on Amazon Bedrock that converts plain-text questions into Sonar queries over more than 900 cloud models and 18 operators, reporting 90 percent lower query costs, 93 percent fewer input tokens and 75 percent lower latency than the initial baseline. The proof of concept loaded the full schema into a single prompt, consuming roughly 2 million input tokens per workload at around 60 seconds per response; the deployed nine-stage pipeline handles thousands of queries per day at 15-second response times.

news.title: How ShipStation Global built an AI IT help desk on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
news.summary: ShipStation Global built Deckhand, an AI IT help desk agent for Slack on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, which resolved 97.5 percent of incoming channel queries with a 96 percent positive feedback rating over three months. In the 12 months before launch employees posted more than 1,500 threads, with more than a fifth of questions arriving outside US business hours from employees in the US, UK, Spain, Poland, Australia and the Philippines; the solution uses a FastAPI and Slack Bolt service on AWS App Runner, a Strands agent using Anthropic's Claude in Amazon Bedrock, and a single AWS Lambda function exposed as MCP tools through AgentCore Gateway.

themes.name: 多模态安全与对抗攻击
themes.summary: 这些论文研究多模态和具身AI系统中的安全与对抗脆弱性，涵盖机器人控制、视觉-语言-动作模型、MLLM、音频智能体和生成式推荐系统。它们分析了越狱、后门、投毒、物理对抗纹理和有害内容规避等攻击，以及包括遗忘、红队测试、可验证检测和安全基准在内的防御。它们的不同之处在于威胁面和评估设置，从场景语义和记忆形成到机器人面部、导航碰撞和工具调用伦理。

themes.name: 智能体Harness自我进化
themes.summary: 这些论文研究智能体harness——管理输入、工具、记忆和执行的外部脚手架——通过反馈引导的迭代修改实现自我进化。它们提出了多种方法，如预测改进模型、harness原生训练循环、测量门控进化、多目标组合和递归harness，同时提供基准和诊断研究，以测试增益是否反映可重用过程而非任务特定修复。关键区别包括单智能体与多智能体、所用反馈类型（结果、过程或证据）以及编码、视频和办公任务等应用领域。

themes.name: 模型合并与压缩
themes.summary: 该主题涵盖微调模型合并以及通过剪枝、量化、低秩近似和无损编码压缩大模型的方法。论文因目标架构（如专家混合、LoRA、视觉Transformer、视频自编码器）以及是否关注权重空间合并、训练后压缩或硬件感知编解码器放置而不同。一些研究还考察这些操作的鲁棒性、校准或安全方面。

themes.name: 视觉-语言-动作机器人策略
themes.summary: 该主题的论文构建视觉-语言-动作策略，将视觉观测和语言指令映射到连续机器人动作，涵盖操作、导航和驾驶。它们的不同之处在于干预位置：一些重塑表示或训练目标（感知-动作桥接、分层自我精化、精度强制、力专业化），另一些改进推理和协调（测试时验证采样、异步执行、多智能体团队的学习适配器），还有一些将VLM推理嵌入规划或导航。多篇论文关注将所学技能泛化到新任务、场景或物体配置。

themes.name: 用于具身控制的世界动作模型
themes.summary: 该主题的论文构建世界模型，预测未来潜在或视觉状态，并将该预测与动作生成相结合，用于具身控制，涵盖机器人操作、GUI智能体、驾驶和手术机器人。它们在以下方面有所不同：未来如何表示（高斯混合潜在预测、谱相似性核、辛哈密顿流、离散视觉token或视频生成），动作如何被条件化或解码（潜在桥接查询、分块流匹配、单步动作生成、分层多时间尺度设计），以及它们优先考虑什么，如记忆和长时域可靠性、因果而非仅仅合理的未来、本体感觉闭环策略评估或降低延迟。

themes.name: 长时域智能体任务基准
themes.summary: 这些论文构建基准，测试LLM智能体能否在扩展工作流中保持连贯的、使用工具的动作，涵盖终端操作、科学数据策展、因果调查、业务请求交付、多数据库查询、记忆维护、生存沙盒以及协议安全的多智能体协调。它们侧重点不同：一些奖励过程级持续进展而非最终通过，一些强调可执行任务契约、记忆表示决策或可验证性技能组合，另一些评估端到端协议风险和鲁棒性。多篇还考察环境保真度和评分有效性，从重新执行编码智能体评估到将智能体置于真实技能规范和交互式物理环境中。

themes.name: 共形预测与不确定性
themes.summary: 这些论文研究不确定性量化和校准，提出共形预测、校准决策模型和有限样本控制等方法以实现可靠预测。它们在应用领域（LLM评判、影像组学、机器人导航、信号时序逻辑）和技术重点上有所不同，例如无分布覆盖、序贯检验或预测集的最优传输。

themes.name: 测试时计算与推理扩展
themes.summary: 这些论文探索通过在推理时分配额外计算来提高模型性能的方法，涵盖循环Transformer中的自适应深度、时间序列和视觉-语言-动作模型的测试时适应、连续生成的验证器引导扩展以及用于高效MoE推理的推测解码。它们的不同之处在于适应模型架构、解码策略还是事后验证器，以及目标模态和约束，如能效、内存限制和实时全双工语音。一些关注倾斜温度等理论解码规则，而另一些将测试时收益整合到模型本身。

themes.name: Flow Matching生成模型
themes.summary: 这些论文发展流匹配及相关的连续时间生成模型，用于虚拟细胞扰动预测、fMRI编码与合成、环肽设计、音频编解码器转换、海洋建模和少步3D生成等多种任务。它们通过扩展流匹配而有所不同，包括后验不确定性、逐token无分类器引导、受限推理时最优控制、采样误差校正、无反向传播的均衡传播训练或薛定谔桥输运。

themes.name: 人形机器人运动与全身控制
themes.summary: 这些论文为人形机器人开发全身控制器和运动策略，涵盖自由空间运动跟踪、无运动先验的地形穿越、竞技乒乓球、协作操作、高速冲刺和刚柔混合连杆，以及相关的四足运动-操作。它们的不同之处在于是否依赖重定向的运动捕捉先验还是学习或基于规划器的参考，以及控制接口，如物体交互层、着陆目标和指挥官-执行者层级。

themes.name: KV Cache压缩与重用
themes.summary: 这些论文压缩或重用KV cache，以减少长上下文自回归生成中的内存和计算，涵盖LLM、视频、边缘和多智能体环境。它们在技术上有所不同——量化、驱逐、整合、跨模型迁移或修复——以及所解决的挑战，如错误累积、行为保持和跨模型不兼容。

themes.name: 扩散语言模型
themes.summary: 这些论文研究用于并行文本生成的扩散语言模型（DLM），解决其在较少采样步骤下的退化、高效时间步放置以及通过锚点的可控性。它们还将该范式扩展到通过连续比特流扩散进行多模态共同生成，以及通过受限扩散智能体保障智能体工作流。它们的侧重点不同：一些提出粗到细建模等生成框架，而另一些分析优化、安全执行或统一多模态训练。

highlights.title: DoSA: Dots Sparse Attention
highlights.why: 提出无损条件稀疏注意力，最高加速2.74x，显著提升LLM推理效率。
highlights.key_result: 我们的GPU实现将完整Indexer在英语、中文和代码工作负载上相对于SGLang最高加速2.74倍，相对于LiteTopK最高加速1.69倍。在GLM-5.2和DeepSeek-V3.2上的端到端评估分别实现相对于两个基线最高1.94和1.50的首token时间加速。
evidence: Our GPU implementation accelerates the complete Indexer by up to 2.74 over SGLang and 1.69 over LiteTopK across English, Chinese, and code workloads.
End-to-end evaluation on GLM-5.2 and DeepSeek-V3.2 achieves up to 1.94 and 1.50 time-to-first-token speedups over the two baselines, respectively.

highlights.title: PANINI-DR: Controlled Deep Research through Generative Semantic Workspaces
highlights.authors: M. Yigit Turali, Shreyas Rajesh, M. Efe Lorasdagi et al.
highlights.why: PANINI-DR在深度研究基准上取得最强平均性能，是受控多智能体研究中的显著进展。
highlights.key_result: Panini-DR在BrowseComp-Plus、FRAMES和MoNaCo上相对于七个最先进的深度研究harness取得了最强平均性能，在BrowseComp-Plus上达到73.3%的准确率，比次优harness高出16.0个百分点，其优势在困难问题上最强，回答数量接近次优harness的两倍。
evidence: We evaluate Panini-DR on BrowseComp-Plus, FRAMES, and MoNaCo against seven state-of-the-art deep-research harnesses, all using a shared language-model backbone and frozen corpora. Panini-DR achieves the strongest average performance across the three benchmarks. On BrowseComp-Plus, Panini-DR achieves 73.3% accuracy, outperforming the next-best harness by 16.0 percentage points. Its advantage is strongest on hard questions, where it answers nearly twice as many as the next-best harness.

Panini-DR has the best average across the three benchmarks, and its advantage is largest on the hardest questions (Table ). Because all systems share the backbone and retrieval service, these differences come from the harnesses. On the BCP hard group, which ReAct agents solve least often, Panini-DR nearly doubles SLEUTH's accuracy.

highlights.title: Refuses in Chat, Complies with Arms: LLM Refusal Does Not Survive Robot Control
highlights.authors: Edward Sun, Christopher Leet, Sravanthi Machcha et al.
highlights.why: 表明当模型控制机器人时LLM拒绝行为崩溃，这是跨具身智能的关键安全失败。
highlights.key_result: 在双臂YAM臂机器人的MuJoCo仿真孪生中，一旦模型控制机器人，拒绝率从文本请求的73%下降到18--25%，即使告知物体是什么。在物理机器人上，六个采用末端执行器控制的模型在612次试验中拒绝率为18%，仿真中为19%；三个采用关节控制的模型在252次试验中拒绝率为41%，仿真中为31%。
evidence: In a MuJoCo simulation twin of a bimanual YAM arm robot, refusal falls from 73% of text requests to 18--25% once the model controls the robot, even when it is told what the objects are.
On the physical robot, six models with end-effector control refused 18% of 612\ trials against 19% in sim, and three with joint control refused 41% of 252\ against 31%.

highlights.title: REPRO: Reflective Evolutionary Prompt Optimizer for Automated LLM Red-Teaming
highlights.why: 通过黑盒进化红队测试，在所有评估的LLM上达到100%攻击成功率，这是一个令人警醒的安全结果。
highlights.key_result: 在我们的协议下，REPRO在单轮内对每个评估目标达到100%攻击成功率（ASR），每个行为的中位目标查询数为24。在我们的协议下，REPRO在AdvBench、JailbreakBench和HarmBench上对来自11个家族的36个目标模型达到100% ASR，每个行为的中位目标查询数为24。
evidence: Under our protocol REPRO reaches 100% attack success rate (ASR) on every evaluated target in a single turn, at a median of 24 target queries per behavior.

Measured across 211 behaviors spanning five target models, REPRO terminates with a median of 24 target queries per behavior, with over half of behaviors completing within 24 queries, compared to up to 10,000 target queries per behavior for prior gray-box state of the art.

Under our protocol, REPRO reaches 100% ASR on AdvBench, JailbreakBench, and HarmBench across 36 target models from 11 families, with a median of 24 target queries per behavior and only a compressed open-weight reflective model on a single consumer GPU.

highlights.title: A Plausible Future Is Not a Causal Future: Can Video Models Generate How the World Unfolds?
highlights.authors: Jialiang Li, Zhengning Xu, Zongyang Ma et al.
highlights.theme: World Action Models for Embodied Control
highlights.why: 提供细致证据表明视频模型生成合理但因果不连贯的未来，质疑其作为世界模型的使用。
highlights.key_result: 在Level 1设置下，模型平均Spatial IoU达到0.194，而Strict ST-IoU仅为0.043；随着未来事件规范从Level 1增加到Level 3，模型平均VQA Overall从0.193上升到0.325，而Strict ST-IoU从0.043增加到0.067。大多数审计失败是基础性的：84.4%的最早失败是基础性的，而只有15.6%首次出现在后续过程维度。
evidence: Under the Level 1 setting, the model-average Spatial IoU reaches 0.194, whereas Strict ST-IoU is only 0.043 (Figure , left).
As future-event specification increases from Level 1 to Level 3, model-average VQA Overall rises from 0.193 to 0.325, while Strict ST-IoU increases from 0.043 to 0.067 (Figure , right).
As shown in Figure , 84.4% of earliest failures are foundational, while only 15.6% first occur at the later process dimensions.

highlights.title: Harness^2: Recursive Agent Harnessing for an Open World
highlights.authors: Ruiyao Xu, Yanfei Chen, Zhongying CuiZhu et al.
highlights.why: 引入面向开放世界的递归harness自我改进，解决智能体适应中的一个关键挑战。
highlights.key_result: 在三个专业基准和四种模型-harness配置中，单次改进步骤持续使GLM-5和Gemini 3.5 Flash相对于其基础harness有所提升，在WorkBuddy-Bench上最多提高11.5分，在JobBench上提高4.5分，在LAB上提高11.8个百分点，并且随着任务级递归预算增加还有进一步提升。
evidence: Across three professional benchmarks and four model--harness configurations, a single step consistently improves GLM-5 and Gemini 3.5 Flash over their base harnesses, yielding gains of up to 11.5 points on WorkBuddy-Bench, 4.5 points on JobBench, and 11.8 percentage points on LAB, with further gains as the task-level recursion budget increases.

One contrastive step improves performance on all three benchmarks in every configuration, with gains of up to 11.5 points on WorkBuddy-Bench, 4.5 points on JobBench, and 11.8 percentage points in LAB Partial pass rate.

On WorkBuddy-Bench, Harness2 raises GLM-5's average score by 11.5 points under OpenCode, the largest one-step improvement over the base harness on this benchmark. The same pattern extends to JobBench and LAB, where gains reach 4.5 points and 11.8 percentage points in Partial pass rate, respectively.

highlights.title: RoboHarness: A Simple Harness Outperforms VLA and World Actions Models
highlights.authors: Bince Qu, Wei Chen, Bo Zhang
highlights.why: 声称一个简单的harness优于最先进的VLA模型，挑战了主流的动作学习范式。
highlights.key_result: 使用RoboHarness，Qwen3.8-Flash-Next在BEHAVIOR Challenge 2025任务上优于最先进的VLA模型。RoboHarness得分不使用机器人训练集，仍达到68--86分。
evidence: With RoboHarness, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next outperforms state-of-the-art VLA models on BEHAVIOR Challenge 2025 tasks .
The RoboHarness points use no robot training set and still score 68--86.

highlights.title: Long-Horizon-Terminal-Bench 2.0: Automating Diverse Task Construction and Measuring Sustained Agent Progress
highlights.authors: Zongxia Li, Zhongzhi Li, Yucheng Shi et al.
highlights.why: 通过自动化构建和更长时域扩展基准，使持续智能体进展可测量。
highlights.key_result: LHTB 2.0 contains 77 tasks across 13 domains and eight task types, preserving the 46 original tasks and adding 31. Across 1,145 scored model-task runs from 15 frontier models, GPT-6-astra leads with dense mean reward 0.69 and 37 tasks at R at least 0.95, and on the 30 reconstruction tasks binary verifier scores average 0.221 whereas dense ladder scores average 0.653.
evidence: We present Long-Horizon-Terminal-Bench 2.0 (LHTB 2.0), an extension of Long-Horizon-Terminal-Bench that preserves its 46 original tasks while correcting task and evaluation-infrastructure defects and extending 31 tasks. LHTB 2.0 contains 77 tasks across 13 domains and eight task types.

Across 1,145 scored model-task runs from 15 frontier models, GPT-6-astra leads with dense mean reward 0.69 and 37 tasks at R at least 0.95, followed by GPT-5.6-sol with dense mean reward 0.67 and 32 tasks at the same threshold.
On the 30 reconstruction tasks, binary verifier scores average 0.221, whereas dense ladder scores average 0.653, showing that outcome-only evaluation discards substantial intermediate progress.

Across 15 frontier models evaluated with a shared terminus-2 agent, the strongest model, GPT-6-astra, resolves only 48.1% of tasks (37/77) at R 0.95, while only 192 of 1,145 scored runs (16.8%) pass overall.

news.title: Higgsfield takes AI video from 1 minute to over 10
news.summary: Higgsfield AI报告称，使用GPT-6 Astra后，用户创建的视频从最长约1分钟延长到超过10分钟，而且GPT-Image-2.5能够可靠地在图像上渲染文本和信息图。该公司以约200名创意人员和100名工程师构建产品，称其YouTube频道拥有几乎half a million订阅者，并致力于通过GPT-Live-1实现“语音生成电影”。

news.title: Developing Gemini 4 Argon responsibly and safely
news.summary: Google DeepMind published its safety and security approach for Gemini 4 Argon, which it says solved all 12 end-to-end simulated cyberattack scenarios versus five for the previous generation, with adversarial-set violations reduced nearly twofold. It describes three layers of real-time protection (input screening, internal introspection via activation probes, and continuous monitoring) and cites Wiz using Argon to uncover a critical bug in hospital software affecting hundreds of thousands of patient records, with the Fairwind Program expanding to more trusted cyber defenders.

news.title: Gemini 4 Argon for Robotics
news.summary: Google DeepMind reports Gemini 4 Argon scores 87% on the Embodied Reasoning (ERQA) benchmark, outperforming other frontier models using pure reasoning. The post lists robotics prompts including controlling a Boston Dynamics Spot (12-DoF legs + 6-DoF arm), retargeting human video onto a 76-DoF bimanual humanoid with 22-DoF five-fingered hands, arranging five Scrabble tiles (G, R, A, N, O), and verifying 6/6 target knockdown in a mujoco_warp scene exported as a Blender 4.5 Cycles render.

news.title: Gemini 4 Argon: Built to solve your hardest problems

news.title: All Systems Go: Global PC App Ecosystem Ready for NVIDIA RTX Spark
